A backend engineer moving toward data and machine learning: the same languages and data stores, a different craft.
A mobile developer moving toward product design: close to the interface, far from the research and critique practice.
An operations engineer moving into security: shared systems and monitoring skills, without the threat-analysis work.
A product manager taking a delivery role: the planning overlaps, the scheduling and risk-register practice does not.
A product designer moving to brand and visual work: shared tools, a different discipline.
A support specialist moving into sales: strong customer contact, no quota or pipeline history.
An administrative specialist moving into human resources: records and scheduling carry over, employee relations does not.
An accountant moving into project management: budgets and reporting carry over, scheduling and vendor work do not.
A nurse applying for a medical assistant role: the clinical skills overlap and the licence level differs.
A teacher moving into social services: work with families carries over, casework and service planning do not.
An electrician moving to heating and cooling service: the electrical work carries over, refrigerant work does not.
A carpentry foreman moving to project management: crews and plans carry over, contracts and cost tracking do not.
